06. Food Management and PDS 
 
 
 
 6.1 Food Security System in the State 
Under the National Food Security Act, the Government is committed to ensuring the 
availability of food grains to poor and eligible families free of cost or at subsidized rates. For this 
purpose, ration cards have been issued to selected eligible families, who are being benefitted through 
the digital Public Distribution System. In the State, as of December 2025, a total of 78,510 fair price 
shops are operating, of which 67,114 are in rural areas and 11,396 in urban areas. By December 
2025, a total of 362.35 Lakh ration cards had been issued in the State, including 40.85 Lakh 
families (11.27%) under the Antyodaya category and 321.50 Lakh families (88.73%) under the 
eligible household category, all covered under the provisions of the Act.

Since 2020-21, under the One Nation-One Ration Card scheme, inter-state portability 
has benefitted a growing number of ration card holders. Beneficiaries in Uttar Pradesh 
rose from 8.88 Lakh in 2021-22 to 38.12 Lakh in 2024-25, a 4.29-fold increase in 
three years. In the first nine months of 2025-26, 28.03 Lakh people were benefitted. 
Overall, since inception, 1.12 Crore UP ration card holders in other States and 1.88 
Lakh from other States in UP have availed the scheme. 
The total number of PDS shops is 78,510, of which 22.9 percent are allotted to women. 
As of 31 December 2025, the number of Antyodaya ration card holder families in the 
State stood at 40.85 Lakh, which is 10.06 percent of the estimated total 4.06 Crore 
families for 2025. 
Under the multipurpose initiative of the ‘Model Fair Price Shop’, up to 31 January
2026, a total of 7,481 Annapurna Bhavans has been constructed, where along with 
ration distribution, CSC services are also being operated. 
The CPI-based inflation rate, with continuous decline after COVID, reached (-)1.71 by 
October 2025 in 2025-26, as a result of which inflation was controlled, purchasing 
power increased, and improvement was reflected in the demand-based economy. 
The latest published Multidimensional Poverty (Headcount Ratio Assessment) was 
42.59 percent in 2013-14, which rapidly declined to 17.40 percent in 2022-23. During 
this period, the highest number of 5.94 Crore people in the State came out of poverty.

Uttar Pradesh received foodgrains in other states, while 0.68 Lakh beneficiaries from other states 
accessed foodgrains in Uttar Pradesh; meanwhile, 279.22 Lakh beneficiaries utilized intra-district

serves as a significant support in strengthening their livelihood. 
 
6.2 Minimum Support Price (MSP) and Procurement Status of 
Major Foodgrain Crops in Uttar Pradesh 
An important dimension of food security is ensuring that the government’s “food basket” 
remains adequately stocked with foodgrains. It is noteworthy that although Uttar Pradesh accounts 
for only about 13.5% of the country’s total cropped area, the state contributes nearly 20.6% to India’s 
total foodgrain production, thereby ranking first in the nation. Since the arrival of crops in each 
season generally leads to a decline in their prices in open markets, the government protects farmers 
from potential losses by fixing Minimum Support Prices (MSP) and undertaking procurement of their 
produce. 
In the Rabi marketing year 2017-18, the Minimum Support Price (MSP) for wheat was Rs. 
1,625 per quintal, which by 2025-26 (the ninth year) had increased by 49.23% to Rs. 2,425 per 
quintal. In 2017-18, 8.00 Lakh farmers benefited, whereas in 2025-26 procurement of 10.27 Lakh 
metric tons of wheat ensured farmer benefits. Data from 2024-25 and 2025-26 clearly show that, 
since wheat prices in open markets remained higher, farmers received returns above MSP. Thus, the 
objective of MSP to guarantee fair value and protect farmers from losses was effectively realized.

Nutrition Security Initiative in Uttar Pradesh 
through Fortified Rice 
Since August 2023, fortified rice has been distributed across all districts 
of Uttar Pradesh under the NFSA and other welfare schemes. This fortified 
rice is enriched with essential nutrients such as Vitamin B12, folic acid, 
and iron. To ensure quality supply to the public, a three-tier quality control 
system has been established: first, testing of premix against FRK 
standards; second, verification through FSSAI-notified laboratories; and 
third, inspection by technical staff of the Food Corporation of India at the 
time of distribution. In the procurement session 2023-24, a total of 36.28 
Lakh metric tonnes of fortified rice was delivered to the central pool, 
which increased to 39.00 Lakh metric tonnes in 2024-25, representing a 
7.5% rise in one year. In 2025-26, up to December, 10.88 Lakh metric 
tonnes of fortified rice have been supplied to the central pool. 
Under the pilot project, following the distribution of fortified rice in 
Chandauli district, an evaluation was conducted through the World Food 
Programme (WFP). The results were significant, showing a marked 
reduction in the prevalence of anaemia among these demographic groups, 
with baseline data from 2021 compared to endline data from 2023. 
✓Among children aged 6-59 months, prevalence declined from 65.7% to 
58.2%, showing a 7.5 percentage point reduction. 
✓Among women aged 15-49 years, prevalence decreased from 
48.7% to 40.7%, reflecting an 8-percentage point reduction. 
✓Among men aged 15-49 years, prevalence fell from 32.9% to 
28.3%, indicating a 4.6 percentage point reduction.

6.3 Pradhan Mantri Ujjwala Yojana: Smokeless Fuel in Every 
Kitchen- Illuminating Happiness Among Women 
The government has fulfilled its commitment to provide clean fuel to poor families by 
implementing this welfare scheme. Under the Pradhan Mantri Ujjwala Yojana, free gas connections 
are being provided in the name of the woman of the household. Each beneficiary of the scheme 
receives LPG cylinders at Rs. 840 per cylinder, against which a subsidy of Rs. 335.19 is directly 
credited to their bank account. 
In addition, two free cylinder refills are provided every year with the objective of promoting 
the use of LPG and fostering the habit of adopting clean fuel. Under the scheme, in the first phase of 
2024-25 (from October 1, 2024 to December 31, 2024), 88.60 Lakh beneficiaries received free refill 
cylinders, while in the second phase (from January 1, 2025 to March 31, 2025), 90.36 Lakh 
beneficiaries were covered. In the first phase of 2025-26 (from October 1, 2025 to December 31, 
2025), 89.44 Lakh beneficiaries received free refill cylinders. 
Since the commencement of the scheme in the year 2018-19, 185 Lakh Ujjwala gas 
connections have been provided so far. This scheme has proved to be a milestone from the point of 
view of the health and convenience of targeted eligible families, especially rural women. Through 
this scheme, while the social dignity of women has increased, there has also been a rise in the use of 
clean fuel among women, and the availability of smoke-free kitchens has relieved them from the 
harmful effects on their health. 
6.4 Women’s Empowerment through the Public Distribution 
System 
Recognizing the vital role of women in food management, the state government has instituted 
a system whereby the woman of the household is considered the head of the family, and ration cards 
are issued in her name. In addition, priority is given to women’s self-help groups in the allocation of 
Public Distribution System (PDS) shops. This decision marks a significant step toward women’s 
empowerment, enabling them to become self-reliant and fostering entrepreneurship. As of December

110 
31, 2025, a total of 4,020 fair price shops has been allotted to women’s self-help groups, including 
3,979 in rural areas and 41 in urban areas. Across the state, 18,032 women dealers have been engaged, 
of whom 22.3% are members of self-help groups. This initiative has brought about social 
transformation by enhancing women’s experience in business management, property ownership, and 
employment generation, while also strengthening their decision-making capacity, mobility, social 
networks, and self-confidence.

Annapurna Bhavan: Model Fair Price Shop as a 
Multipurpose Initiative 
In every district of the state, the system of single-stage doorstep 
delivery has been implemented, ensuring that foodgrains are 
transported directly from warehouses to ration shops. This has 
curtailed pilferage and black marketing while saving time and 
resources. 
In 2023-24, the government decided to construct 75 Annapurna 
Bhavans annually in each district. Each building is designed with 
two large halls and a 4-foot-wide veranda for beneficiaries’ 
waiting area. One hall is used for foodgrain distribution, while the 
other is utilized for CSC operations and the sale of essential 
commodities. Construction during 2023-24 and 2024-25 was 
carried out under MGNREGA convergence, while for 2025-26, a 
separate budget allocation of Rs. 200 Crore has been made. 
From 2023-24 up to December 2025, a total of 7,481 Annapurna 
Bhavans has been constructed, while 5,522 are under 
construction. 
Model fair price shops have been integrated with broadband and 
CSC services under PM-WANI. This enables rural citizens to 
access local services such as income, caste, and residence 
certificates, as well as electricity bill payments.

6.6 Food Service Management in the State 
 
Under food service management, proper storage of food grains is a primary and important 
dimension, enabling farmers to preserve their produce safely even during adverse weather conditions. 
In recent years, with the strengthening of the state’s supply chain, digital systems have been adopted 
to ensure the swift execution of activities, thereby guaranteeing timely availability of food grains to 
the public. In Uttar Pradesh, a total of 234 warehouses (152 of the State Warehousing Corporation, 
48 of the Indian Warehousing Corporation and 34 of the Central Warehousing Corporation) were 
operational in 2017-18, which increased by 23.93% to 290 warehouses (182 of the State Warehousing 
Corporation, 48 of the Indian Warehousing Corporation, and 60 of the Central Warehousing 
Corporation) in 2024-25. The average storage capacity of warehouses in the state was 59.43 Lakh 
metric tons in 2017-18, which has risen by 14.49% to 68.04 Lakh metric tons in 2024-25. 
 
Under the National Agriculture Development Scheme, out of 103 approved rural warehouses 
with a capacity of 100 metric tons, construction of 88 has been completed while the rest are under 
progress; similarly, out of 24 approved rural warehouses with a capacity of 250 metric tons, 
construction of 6 has been completed and the remaining are still under construction. In addition, 
within the PCF, out of 11 approved rural warehouses aimed at creating a capacity of 11,800 metric 
tons, construction of 5 has been completed while the others are in progress. Under the world’s largest 
Digital Platform for Farmers: A Significant Initiative 
Online Registration and Verification of Farmers- Farmers are being registered online on the portal of the Food 
and Civil Supplies Department for the sale of their produce. Through this system, the land area and agricultural 
produce are verified online via the Revenue Department’s land records portal, thereby adopting a swift and 
transparent arrangement for sales. This process ensures that farmers receive the benefits of the Minimum Support 
Price scheme in a timely manner while also guaranteeing a transparent payment mechanism. Uttar Pradesh is the 
leading state in the country to implement this arrangement. 
Integration of e Procurement Portal and Revenue Department’s Land Records Portal- The e Procurement (e 
Uparjan) portal and the Revenue Department’s land records portal have been integrated. At procurement Centres, 
food grains are purchased from farmers only after Aadhaar based biometric verification through e PoS machines. 
GPS Tracking and Monitoring of Vehicles- An online dispatch system has been implemented to transport food 
grains purchased from procurement Centres and custom-milled rice to FCI depots. By linking the Food and Civil 
Supplies portal with the Ministry of Transport’s portal, GPS tracking and monitoring of vehicles is ensured. 
Agri stack Portal: For the Kharif marketing year 2025-26, a system of self-verification has also been introduced 
on the Agri stack portal, based on the data available there and the e-investigation records.

Society in Mirzapur was selected as a pilot project, whose construction was completed in December

Under food service management, the state has initiated the ‘Krishak Prasar and Pest Control 
Service’ scheme to modernize warehouses with advanced technologies and to support farmers in 
grain storage and protection. Under this scheme, 29,401 farmers were trained in 2021-22, which 
increased by 74.6% to 51,337 in 2022-23, and further rose by 184.9% to 83,781 in 2024-25. This 
consistent rise in farmer training reflects their growing awareness, enabling them to store their 
produce properly and sell it when necessary or when market prices are favourable. The warehouses 
have also been registered with the Warehousing Development and Regulatory Authority (WDRA). 
 
 This process ensures that when farmers properly store their produce, a negotiable 
warehouse receipt is issued, on the basis of which they can obtain loans from banks as needed 
and sell their produce later when market prices are higher. Under the supervision of the Food 
Corporation of India, the construction agency HLC has selected Hamirpur, Lalitpur, and 
Pilibhit in Uttar Pradesh for the construction of steel silos, each with a capacity of 50,000 
metric tons. In these silos, food grains will remain fully protected through the automatic use 
of pest control measures. 
6.7 Impact of Prices and Inflation 
 In 
the 
continuously 
evolving landscape of the 
economy, fluctuations in 
inflation remain a crucial 
factor, 
as 
inflationary 
pressures directly affect the 
general public while also 
creating imbalances amidst 
ongoing economic reforms. 
To address this, the central 
bank and the government 
carefully implement inflation-control measures by cautiously relaxing their restrictive policies. 
In determining the Consumer Price Index (CPI), food items play a crucial role, and therefore 
retail inflation is considered to be primarily driven by the Consumer Food Price Index (CFPI). In this 
context, an analysis has been presented of the major food items that influence inflation such as cereals 
and cereal products, meat and fish, eggs, milk and milk products, vegetables, pulses, sugar and 
confectionery, spices, etc. along with household and other essential services.
